w1_final.reason: The core facts — an unplanned November 12 cooling-water-pressure loss forcing advanced packaging tools into safe state, reduced saleable-bit output, adjusted customer delivery dates, and a recovery window extending through January 31, 2027 — describe a new operational disruption occurrence not present in any loaded Event. Existing Events cover HBM capacity sold-out status (E15), supply-demand commentary (E28), and HBM4E roadmap (E17), none of which capture this specific interruption event or its output/delivery consequences.

candidates.proposition: An unexpected loss of cooling-water pressure in a shared utility loop at a critical advanced-packaging area at Micron's Boise site required Micron to place a defined group of advanced packaging tools into a controlled safe state on the late night of November 12, 2026. The interruption was not part of a planned maintenance event.

The affected advanced-packaging area serves selected high-bandwidth-memory and server-memory customer programs; during the interruption, new material was not released into the defined packaging sequence, and material already in the sequence was held under normal process controls.

The incident removed available capacity from a critical packaging step used by the affected HBM and server-memory programs, while other manufacturing and packaging areas at the site continued to operate.
Following its initial site and process review, Micron reduced its expected saleable-bit output for the affected packages during the current recovery period.

Micron adjusted delivery dates for a limited set of customer commitments that had been scheduled to leave the affected packaging sequence before the end of December 2026, and has informed the relevant customers directly while working with them on revised delivery dates.

Micron stated it is not treating the change as a routine sequencing adjustment because the affected output cannot be recovered simply by moving material through the normal weekly maintenance calendar.

Micron expects the physical repair work at the affected utility loop to conclude during the week of November 18, 2026, followed by a staged equipment return, qualification lots, and controlled restoration of normal release volumes.

Based on the current engineering plan, the affected advanced-packaging area is expected to remain in recovery through January 31, 2027, a window extending beyond the site's ordinary planned-maintenance interval.

Micron did not attribute the interruption to demand conditions, customer specifications, or a product-quality issue, describing it instead as an operational disruption at a key manufacturing-support node.

All material held during the interruption will remain subject to standard release controls before shipment, and customer teams have received the same recovery timetable used by the site, including the expected staged return of tools and the period during which saleable output remains below the pre-interruption plan.
